title: Mara and the Terminal
premise: Juniper Blackwood tends the Genesis Vault, a seed archive meant for colonists not yet born, on Meridian Station—a terraforming colony Earth quietly wrote off after a catastrophic 'accident' that never happened. When the station's children begin sharing a recurring dream of fire and sealed doors—including a girl named Mara who remembers things she was never told—Juniper realizes the official records were rewritten to bury a massacre of the first generation. As Earth's final transmission loop counts down to permanent silence, Juniper must help the children recover buried evidence in the station's dead sectors and broadcast the truth before the loop ends. He succeeds at terrible cost: the truth escapes, but Juniper stays behind with the dying station so the children can carry it home.
about_author: Silas Voss is the pen name of a former hydrologist who spent six years working remote environmental monitoring stations before turning to fiction. They write slow-burn science fiction about people who keep systems running long after anyone remembers why.

chapters.title: The Garden for No One
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. He tends the Genesis Vault's seedlings alone, logging plant data and the colony's dwindling population into a journal no one reads. Establishes the forgotten station, his routine invisibility, and the countdown clock of Earth's transmission loop. Emotional beat: quiet grief disguised as diligence.

chapters.title: Children of the Quiet Wing
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. He delivers nutrient paste to the station's remaining families and notices the children whispering about 'the burning door.' Mara, sharp-eyed and unafraid of him, asks what the vault was really built for. Emotional beat: unease—the first crack in normalcy.

chapters.title: Same Dream, Different Beds
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The dream recurs: orange light, a corridor sealing, names being called through metal. Mara compares notes with other children and finds they all hear the same name—her mother's. Emotional beat: dread blooming into resolve.

chapters.title: Records Say Otherwise
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. He pulls the station archive to fact-check the children's details and finds the incident logs immaculate, too immaculate—gaps papered over with boilerplate. His own older personal backups contradict them. Emotional beat: the vertigo of realizing the record itself is lying.

chapters.title: What the Old Woman Kept
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Elder technician Sefa, one of three first-generation survivors, gives Juniper a physical keyring and warns him that the last audit was written by the men who did it. Emotional beat: inherited guilt passed hand to hand.

chapters.title: Down in the Dead Sectors
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. He and Mara descend into unpowered sections where the air recyclers died years ago. They find a sealed med-bay door scorched from the inside. Emotional beat: claustrophobic horror made intimate by Mara's calm.

chapters.title: The Loop Ends in Forty Days
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. He calculates Earth's transmission loop will terminate in forty days; after that, no uplink exists. He must decide whether to stay invisible or act. Emotional beat: the cost of survival named aloud.

chapters.title: Mara Remembers Fire
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Under pressure from adults demanding the children stop talking, Mara recalls fragments she couldn't have witnessed—her mother's voice counting evacuation numbers. She understands she carries testimony. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Sefa's Confession
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. She admits she helped seal the doors during the 'quarantine,' believing orders, and has spent twenty years tending the survivors' graves in the compost rows. Emotional beat: shame as a form of penance—and a map to the black box.

chapters.title: The Black Box Problem
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The flight recorder proving the massacre sits in the crashed lander at the crater rim, outside walkable range, and the station's last shuttle was cannibalized. Emotional beat: hope meeting logistics.

chapters.title: Building a Ghost Ship
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Juniper, Sefa, and the older teens strip the vault's maintenance drones to build a retrieval rig, hiding the work inside legitimate garden telemetry. Emotional beat: conspiracy as community—the invisible becoming a crew.

chapters.title: The Administrator Notices
chapters.summary: Administrator Kell's POV. Kell, complicit but weary, detects the drone thefts and faces his own choice: report to Earth's dying oversight AI or let it slide. Emotional beat: cowardice wrestling with conscience.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Kindness
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Kell confronts Juniper gently, offering him transfer off-station in exchange for silence. Juniper refuses, and Kell, shaken, doesn't report him—but doesn't help either. Emotional beat: the seduction of escape declined.

chapters.title: Launch Window
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The rig launches toward the crater during a dust storm window. Mara runs telemetry from the vault while the children keep watch. Emotional beat: held breath, collective courage.

chapters.title: Signal from the Wreck
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The rig reaches the lander and begins pulling the recorder, but storm damage degrades the link halfway through download. Emotional beat: triumph curdling into desperation.

chapters.title: Kell Breaks
chapters.summary: Kell's POV. Watching the download fail, Kell finally acts—he reroutes the station's reserve power to the array, damning himself in the logs. Emotional beat: redemption purchased with self-destruction.

chapters.title: What the Recorder Says
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The full recording plays: forty-one voices begging at a sealed door while officials debate 'asset protection.' The children listen to their parents die. Emotional beat: unbearable witness, shared.

chapters.title: Broadcast Against the Clock
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. With hours left in the transmission loop, they must compress the evidence past Earth's censors and aim it at an independent relay. Kell sacrifices himself to hold the antenna alignment manually. Emotional beat: frantic, sacrificial climax.

chapters.title: The Loop Closes
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The transmission goes out seconds before the loop terminates forever. Confirmation will take years, if it comes at all. Emotional beat: faith without guarantee.

chapters.title: Earth Answers, Late
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Months later, a single unscheduled packet arrives: receipt confirmed, inquiry opened. It is both everything and not enough. Emotional beat: justice arriving as paperwork, still real.

chapters.title: Who Stays
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A rescue vessel will come for the children, but the station can only support a skeleton crew during the wait. Juniper volunteers to stay, giving Mara his journal and the vault keys. Emotional beat: inheritance completed.

chapters.title: The Garden for Someone
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, epilogue. From the departing ship, Mara looks back at the station's green-lit dome and begins reading Juniper's journal aloud to the younger children, planting the first seeds in the ship's nursery. Emotional beat: the dead garden blooming elsewhere—survival as continuation.
